title: Your first animation
summary: Draw a ball, turn it into a symbol, send it across the stage with a classic tween, ease it, check the spacing with onion skinning, and export a video.

steps.title: Welcome
steps.text:
In this lesson you will draw a ball and animate it across the stage.

Phoenix has opened a new HD document for it, 1280×720 at 24 frames per second. The white rectangle is the stage: whatever is on it ends up in your video.

Click Next to begin. You can drag this window anywhere.

steps.title: Pick the Oval tool
steps.text: Press O, or click the Oval tool in the toolbox. It shares a slot with the Rectangle: press and hold the slot to choose between them.

steps.title: Choose a color
steps.text:
Click the fill swatch, the solid square at the bottom of the toolbox, and pick a bright color for the ball.

The outlined square beside it is the stroke color. To draw the ball without an outline, uncheck Stroke on the Properties panel's Tool tab.

steps.title: Draw a circle
steps.text: Hold Shift and drag near the left edge of the stage to draw a circle. Shift keeps it round.

steps.title: Switch to the Selection tool
steps.text: Press V, or click the arrow at the top of the toolbox.

steps.title: Select the whole ball
steps.text: Double-click the ball. That selects its fill and its outline together, shown with a fine dot pattern.

steps.title: Turn it into a symbol
steps.text:
Tweens move whole objects, so the ball needs to become a symbol.

Press F8, or choose Modify > Convert to Symbol. Name it Ball, set Type to Graphic, and click OK.

steps.title: Go to frame 24
steps.text: In the timeline, click the cell under frame 24 on the ball's layer. At 24 frames per second that is one second in.

steps.title: Insert a keyframe
steps.text: Press F6, or choose Insert > Timeline > Keyframe. The frames between 1 and 24 fill in, showing that the ball is held across them.

steps.title: Move the ball
steps.text: With the playhead still on frame 24, drag the ball to the right side of the stage.

steps.title: Tween between the keyframes
steps.text:
Right-click any frame between 1 and 24 and choose Classic Tween, or click one and choose Insert > Classic Tween.

The span turns lilac with an arrow: Phoenix now works out the frames in between.

steps.title: Play it
steps.text: Press Enter, or click the play button in the timeline header. Press it again to stop.

steps.title: Pick a frame of the tween
steps.text: Stop playback, then click a frame inside the tween, such as frame 12. Its settings show on the Properties panel's Frame tab.

steps.title: Ease the motion
steps.text:
Real objects speed up and slow down. On the Properties panel's Frame tab, open the Ease list and choose an In Out preset.

Play again: the ball now starts gently and settles into place.

steps.title: Check the spacing
steps.text: Turn on onion skinning with this button, or Alt+Shift+O. Frames before the playhead show in blue and frames after it in green, so you can see how the ball's spacing changes as it eases.

steps.title: Export a video
steps.text: Choose File > Export > Export Movie, set Format to Video and the codec to H.264, and click Export. Phoenix encodes the video itself; nothing else needs installing.

steps.title: Well done
steps.text:
You drew a ball, made it a symbol, tweened and eased it, and exported a movie.

Save your document with Ctrl+S if you want to keep it. Help > Tutorials has more lessons, such as Merge and object drawing and Symbols and editing in place.
